newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific to double Ford traffic in '97.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific to double Ford traffic in '97.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp said Ford Motor Co will double the number of vehicles the carmaker transports via Union Pacific's railroads next year through the auto maker's new "mixing center" distribution system.
Union Pacific said it expects to deliver more than 900,000 Ford vehicles a year to 13 western and southern destinations.

The increase, which begins in January, is the result of a distribution system Ford is implementing to reduce order-to-delivery time. The system places both cars and trucks on trains headed to various destinations at a Ford distribution center in Kansas City, Union Pacific said.

"It would have been impossible for us to win this business if it had not been for the Union Pacific/Southern Pacific merger," the railroad said. "Our single system service and routing efficiencies allowed us to work with Ford to design a distribution system that dramatically improves Ford's finished vehicle delivery capabilities."

Autos and trucks will be mixed in Kansas City at one of Ford's new hub distribution centers, which are designed to reduce transit time. As a result of the award, Union Pacific said, it will be the sole transportation provider to the entire southwestern United States.
